title: Twisted Empyrean Mana Stacking Titan Build Guide
summary: A Titan that stacks maximum mana to convert spell damage into attack damage through Twisted Empyrean, Rathpith Globe and Crown of Eyes, then slams bosses.

seo.title: Twisted Empyrean Mana Stacking Titan Build Guide (PoE2 0.5)
seo.description: Mana-stacking slam Titan using Twisted Empyrean. Real creator video, leveling, gear, sources.

changes: Fourth-batch source-reviewed publication. Cross-verified from official 0.5 patch notes, current creator guides, an independent build guide, a planner, a current gameplay video and community questions.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Twisted Empyrean rewards maximum mana: it scales your damage with mana, and the unique chain (Rathpith Globe granting spell damage, Crown of Eyes converting spell damage to attack damage) lets a Titan slam bosses with what looks like caster power.
This is a verification-first guide. The dependency chain is described from current creator guides; the key risk - empty mana removing both damage and defense - is the actionable core.

sections.title: Pros and Cons
pros: Big single slam bursts once the unique chain is online.
Maximum mana scales both offense and a defensive layer.
Titan natural bulk suits the slam playstyle.
Clear uses a mobile Leap Slam.
cons: Needs several specific uniques to function.
Empty mana removes damage AND defense at once.
One slam rarely one-shots every boss.
High-investment; not a barebones league starter.

sections.title: Is This Build Right For You?
paragraphs: Pick Twisted Empyrean if you enjoy a mana-stacking slam identity and you can source the core uniques (Twisted Empyrean, Rathpith Globe, Crown of Eyes). It is not a starter; it is an endgame project.
If you lack the uniques, run a generic slam Titan first. The build only clicks once the chain is complete.

steps.label: Levels 1-40 - Generic slam
body: Level as a normal slam Warrior with a two-hander. Focus on life and resistances; the unique chain is not online yet.

steps.label: Levels 41-65 - Unique assembly
body: Acquire Twisted Empyrean, then Rathpith Globe and Crown of Eyes as budget allows. Hold a generic slam until the chain is complete.

steps.label: Levels 66+ - Mana stack
body: Stack maximum mana on gear and jewels. Add mana reservation efficiency and the slam supports.

steps.label: Waystones - Endgame
body: Refine crit, resistances and mana. Benchmark on T15 before pushing 200% Delirium content.

whyUse: Main boss damage once mana conversion is online.

mappingBossingDiff: Use for mapping mobility; not the boss burst.

recommendations: Crown of Eyes is the conversion key: it lets spell damage affect your attacks, which is what the Twisted Empyrean chain needs.
Rathpith Globe grants spell damage from maximum mana - a normal roll plus a possible corrupted roll. The corrupted line is bonus, not required.
Twisted Empyrean is the build's namesake unique; it drives the mana-scaling damage. A two-hander baseline works while assembling the rest.
Maximum mana, life, resistances. Stack mana wherever it does not cost a core unique slot.

steps.label: Starter -> Functional
body: Generic slam; cap resistances and life before chasing uniques.

steps.label: Functional -> Endgame
body: Acquire the three core uniques, then stack maximum mana and add slam supports.

steps.label: Endgame -> Luxury
body: Chase perfect mana rolls, crit gear and jewels only after T15 is comfortable.

sections.title: Unique Dependency Chain
paragraphs: Twisted Empyrean (mana scaling) -> maximum mana -> Rathpith Globe (spell damage) -> Crown of Eyes (spell damage to attacks) -> Titan slam amp -> boss debuff -> Hammer of the Gods. Each arrow depends on the prior unique; a missing link collapses the chain.

sections.title: Why Max Mana Matters Twice
paragraphs: Maximum mana feeds the damage conversion AND sits before life as a defensive buffer on this setup. When mana is healthy, you hit hard and survive; when it is empty, you lose both at once.

sections.title: Spell Damage to Attack
paragraphs: Crown of Eyes is what makes caster-style spell damage apply to your attacks. Without it, the Rathpith mana-to-spell-damage step has nothing to convert into slam power.

sections.title: Slam Mechanics
paragraphs: Fist of War and Ancestral Empowerment amplify your slam's committed damage; they reward standing in the slam rather than cancel-casting. Leap Slam is the clear tool, Hammer of the Gods is the boss tool.

sections.title: Mapping Rotation
paragraphs: For normal packs: Leap Slam through safe lanes; the mobility is the clear, not a stationary slam. Save the big slam for rares and bosses.

sections.title: Rare Rotation
paragraphs: For rares: drop Orb of Storms and Warrior Mark, then Hammer of the Gods. Keep moving between slams; do not over-extend into a deadly modifier.

sections.title: Boss Rotation
paragraphs: For bosses: apply the Effigy of Cruelty / Critical Weakness debuff, drop Orb of Storms and Mark, then commit Hammer of the Gods. Verify the sequence in the current client before treating the written order as final, and disengage on telegraphed slams.

sections.title: Titan Ascendancy
paragraphs: Titan's slam and stun bonuses suit a committed-hit playstyle. The ascendancy makes the big slam hit harder and more reliably, which is exactly what this mana-conversion build wants for bosses.

sections.title: Passive Tree Approach
paragraphs: Start with life, resistances and maximum mana nodes, then specialize toward slam and crit as the uniques allow. The tree is read against your mana pool, not copied wholesale.

sections.title: Budget Variants
paragraphs: Before the uniques, run a generic slam Titan - it is a real, playable build. Twisted Empyrean only becomes the headline once Twisted Empyrean, Rathpith Globe and Crown of Eyes are all present.

sections.title: Defensive Layers
paragraphs: Life plus the mana-before-life buffer is the baseline. Because empty mana removes both offense and defense, manage mana uptime as a survival stat, not just a damage stat.

sections.title: Community Voices

entries.label: Reddit - mana drained
entries.statement: Players report that a no-regen map plus the mana costs can leave them with no damage and no buffer at once, confirming the double risk.

entries.label: Forum - rathpith rolls
entries.statement: Question: which Rathpith line is the corrupted bonus. The consensus is the base mana-to-spell-damage roll is required; the extra corrupted line is luxury.

entries.label: Guide comments - defense
entries.statement: Players note that until mana and life are both solved, the build feels squishy because empty mana removes the buffer.

sections.note: Short paraphrases of common community questions and concerns, edited for clarity. Not verbatim quotes.

items.question: What does Twisted Empyrean actually provide?
answer: It scales your damage with maximum mana, which is the engine that the rest of the unique chain amplifies.

items.question: Why does max mana affect both damage and defense?
answer: It drives the damage conversion and also sits as a buffer before life on this setup. Empty mana therefore removes both.

items.question: Can I start this on a low budget?
answer: Not as Twisted Empyrean. Run a generic slam Titan until you have the three core uniques; then the build clicks.

items.question: Does one slam one-shot every boss?
answer: No. 200% Delirium survival conclusions do not generalize; the slam is a strong burst, not a universal delete button.

problems.symptom: No damage and squishy at once
checks: Check mana uptime first - empty mana removes both. Add mana sources / reservation efficiency before changing damage gear.
Run a generic slam Titan until the missing link (typically Crown of Eyes or Rathpith Globe) is acquired; the chain cannot function without it.
